hypothesis: A baseline trained on the target dataset does not test our generalisation claim. Train AKOrN on CLEVR alone, on our exact exposure budget, and evaluate it on all three reserved splits the way our frozen core is evaluated.
changed_variable: which dataset the baseline trains on (CLEVR, not the target), holding exposures, train ids, evaluation ids, grid and evaluation function fixed
success_criterion: our CLEVR-trained core beats the CLEVR-trained AKOrN on all three metrics on all three datasets
outcome: met at seed 0: 9 of 9 cells, and every margin exceeds AKOrN own two-seed spread (0.1339 CLEVR, 0.0535 Tetrominoes, 0.0094 Multi-dSprites)

data.split_manifest_version: fixed320 reserved evaluation, not an independent original-paper TEST split
data.protocol: patch contract: truth quantised to the grid, predictions reduced to the grid by patch majority vote, never expanded to pixels
data.train_ids: the identical 10,000 drawn by np.random.RandomState(2553500).choice(Dataset.train, 10000, replace=False) that the 253 core trained on
data.truth_tensor: Dataset.labels(ids, split) at grid 64, np.repeat-ed x2 to 128 inside the npz; NOT Dataset.pixels / the raw h5 mask

baseline.published_config_deviation: epochs only: CLEVR 300 -> 10, dSprites 50 -> 10, to match 100,000 exposures
baseline.published_exposures_clevr: ~21,000,000 (300 epochs x ~70,000 train images) = 210x this run
baseline.eval_cluster_count: fixed per dataset by eval_obj.py: 4 tetrominoes, 7 dsprites, 11 clevr -- a dataset-level constant, not per-image truth
baseline.seed_note: the first runs went out without --seed and so used AKOrN own default 1234; seed 0 was then trained to match ours. Headline rows are seed 0; the 1234 rows are kept in metrics.csv as a spread, never as a mean.

new_files: benchmark_codes/bg_any.py -- background-rule selection on validation for any hard-partition baseline, same four rules and same selection as sa_bg.py
benchmark_codes/to_grid64.py -- patch majority vote reducing a finer-than-grid partition to the grid
baselines/akorn_clevr_data.py -- our CLEVR splits in AKOrN npz format
baselines/akorn_data128.py -- tetrominoes / multi_dsprites eval frames at 128 with the truth lifted x2
baselines/akorn_val_data.py -- the grid-64-label variants used for the dSprites-trained row
modified_in_clone: eval_dump.py -- a copy of eval_obj.py with shuffle=False in the generic eval loader and a prediction dump appended; eval_obj.py itself untouched

artifacts_note: checkpoints, npz data and logs stay out of git; see artifacts.json
limitations: our side is seed 0 only; the contract judges 3-seed means
AKOrN is two seeds (0 and its default 1234) reported as a spread, not a mean

AKOrN at 1/210 of its published budget is not the model its authors report (published 3-seed means: tetrominoes 88.6+-1.7, dsprites 78.3+-1.3, clevr 91.0+-0.5, on the pixel protocol and the full official test splits)
AKOrN is given a fixed per-dataset cluster count our readout does not get
AKOrN mBO here is not comparable to its published mBO: the truth we feed it is the grid quantisation, not the true pixel mask
fixed320 is a reserved evaluation split, not an independent original-paper test split
next: AKOrN seeds 1 and 2 (7 min per CLEVR run) to turn the spread into a 3-seed mean
decide protocol B for AKOrN: 300 epochs on our 10,000 (~3.5 h) or on the full 70,000 (~24 h)
our own CLEVR seeds 1 and 2 remain the expensive unapproved item; the 0.1339 baseline reseed swing says they are not a formality
own_metric_agreement_fg_ari: ours vs AKOrN own eval_obj.py: <=0.0010 on every cell, exactly 0.0000 where no grid reduction is needed
